decision_evidence.note: github-remote-provider scores higher but is sovereignty-gated as an external side effect; the DWAC North Star controller therefore selects the highest-value autonomous work instead of letting gated work starve it.

rcl_authority_reuse.reason: persistent terminal open and input remain shell execution inside the existing workspace authority boundary; no new external authority is introduced

implementation: Preserve the existing bounded one-shot runCommand API for compatibility.
Add a persistent terminal runtime with session create/list/read/input/resize/close lifecycle and cursor-addressed output evidence.
Prefer a node-pty-compatible provider, using Windows ConPTY when available; fall back to a real POSIX pseudo-terminal through script on non-Windows hosts.
Keep every server-side terminal open/input action behind the existing RCL shell_execute authority gate.
Keep custom shell selection restricted to full_access at the HTTP boundary.
Fix the existing destructive-command guard so the literal rm -rf / case is actually rejected in workspace mode.
Add the prebuilt @lydell/node-pty provider as an optional dependency so unsupported native packaging does not make the entire product uninstallable.

validation.evidence: util-linux script PTY retained cd /tmp across separate writes
create -> input -> read -> close returned posix-script-pty and observed __HTTP_PTY__/tmp
rm -rf / is now rejected with DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND_BLOCKED in workspace mode
injected node-pty-compatible provider verified useConpty=true, write, resize and kill lifecycle

truth_boundaries: Windows ConPTY was not reality-executed on a Windows host in this cycle; only the provider contract path was tested with an injected node-pty-compatible provider.
The optional @lydell/node-pty package installation/native binary was not downloaded or executed in the isolated validation container.

The local HTTP integration harness used an allow-all RCL gate stub; the canonical RCL policy was independently inspected and already contains shell_execute authority, but the full native RCL runtime was not exercised by that harness.
The destructive input filter is a policy guard, not an operating-system sandbox; sovereignty remains enforced by the RCL shell_execute authority boundary.
This cycle closes the persistent terminal runtime/API bottleneck; it does not claim a browser UI conversion to a live terminal emulator.
